summary: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sera and Drepung Monasteries, the Universities of Melbourne and British Columbia, and under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Dilgo Khyentse, Trijang, and Trulshik.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1975–1986) and under Sangye Tenzin Rinpoche, Lopon Tenzin Namdak, and others, serving as the Institute's president (~1986–1991) and a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College (1966), the University of Chicago (1970), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979), and held a post at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 2001–2003).

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1942–1967), Keio University (~1967–1972), the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, and Aichi University.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz worked in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Universities of Florida, Virginia, Ceylon, Cornell, Florida State, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at the University of Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~1991–2001), and Florida State (1993).

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University until ~1931. He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1971–1976), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1971–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1877–1880), Heidelberg University (~1884–1887), and Leipzig University (~1887–1890). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1882–1890) and Toyo University (~1896–1906).

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1959–1965) and Komazawa University (~1965–1969). He held positions at Komazawa University (~1979–1990, 2002–2006), Tomakomai Komazawa (2006–2007), Tsuru (2013–2016), Tohoku Fukushi (2015–2019), and Peking University.
Tetsuo Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Shizuoka University (~1953–1957) and served as an assistant professor at Otani University from ~1969 to 1980.

Tetsuro Watsuji was a philosopher, religious studies scholar, and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1909–1912). He held posts at Toyo, Otani, Hosei, Ryukoku, Kyoto (~1925–1934), and the University of Tokyo (~1934–1949).
Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He held an academic post at Utrecht University, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2000.
Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in the field of history and archaeology who studied under the guidance of V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodor Aufrecht worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1847), where he became Privatdozent in 1850. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1862) and Professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1824–1826). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).
Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1890–1892) under Ernst Windisch, and later studied under Georg Bühler (~1893–1895).

Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg under Peter von Bohlen and Karl Rosenkranz, Bonn under Christian Lassen, and under Eugène Burnouf. He held a chair in Sanskrit at University College London and the University of London (~1852–1872).

Theodor Nöldeke was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Vienna, Berlin, and Leiden, and held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1861–1864) and the University of Kiel (~1864–1872).
Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He received his education at Hopkins School and Yale College (~1816–1820).
